Baltic Exchange Market Report 20 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2633 (66)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4300 (172)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1976 (1)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1422 (7)
Baltic Handysize Index: 754 (13)
CAPESIZE
The market extended its upward momentum at the start of the week, with the BCI 182 5TC advancing by $1,564 to settle just shy of the $39,000 mark at $38,999. While the headline index posted a strong gain, underlying route performance was more nuanced. C5 remained largely flat, edging up only $0.010 to $13.605, while C3 provided the main source of strength, climbing by $1.041 to $33.714. In the Pacific, sentiment was steady but firm, with two miners active on C5. However, despite early offers circulating in the low $14.00s, fixtures ultimately concluded closer to $13.60 levels. In contrast, the Atlantic basin continued to show solid support, underpinned by a tightening tonnage list, particularly for C3 ballasters. Stronger fixtures emerged, including post-index activity last Friday at $33.75 for index and end-May dates. The fronthaul market also saw notable improvement, with a firmer fixture driving C9 up sharply by $3,777 to $66,333. On the macro front, oil volatility returned, with Brent crude rebounding amid ongoing uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, adding a layer of complexity to bunker sentiment.
PANAMAX
A sluggish start to the week across the Panamax markets with a limited number of reported fixtures. In the Atlantic, although we have heard about fresh enquiry for both fronthaul and transatlantic trades it would appear that there is a thin amount of fixing. Offers are still holding firm on the back of last week’s rate push but one cannot ignore the increasing available tonnage list. The Euripides Graecia (82,055 2020) open in Nansha 6 April was reported to have fixed basis delivery Sunda Strait for a trip via East Coast South America to the Far East with grains a $21,500, although a charterer was not reported. In Asia a similar story can be found with cargoes still appearing but with a growing tonnage lineup. With this said, some market participants have hinted that although tonnage appears to be plentiful there are few owners willing to rate and subsequently has a stand-off feeling. The LC Milady (93,758 2011) open Gangavaram 23 April was reported to have fixed a coastal coal trip with redelivery in EC India at $27,000 to Messrs Panbulk. The P5TC reflected this sentiment, increasing slightly by $12 to conclude Monday at $17,785.
SUPRAMAX
A subdued start to the week with many eyes focused on the ever-changing situation from the Middle East. The Atlantic was seen as positional, some saying the recent demand seen from the US Gulf for fronthaul business might have reached a ceiling and rates had eased slightly. Demand remained for trans Atlantic business although again some felt that limited fresh opportunities were being seen from the East Mediterranean. The Asian arena remained balanced although again little fresh information surfaced, as both owners' and charterers watched for any clear direction. The 11TC average started the week up $84 at $17,970.
HANDYSIZE
A typical Monday with limited fresh activity surfacing. The Atlantic remained in positive mode with sustained demand from both the US Gulf and South American areas. The Continent-Mediterranean was described by brokers as remaining fairly steady as fundamentals remained unchanged from last week. Continuing from last week’s gains, Asia gained further ground as prompt tonnage remained tight from the north and better levels of fresh enquiry remained from the south. The 7TC average started the week up $234 at $13,571.

Atlantic
The C Tiger (35,693 2011) open Vlissingen was heard fixed at $15,500 for a scrap run with Weco but no more details came to light. The UBC Houston (38,762 2015) was clean fixed a a packaged lumber requirement to the US Gulf from Germany at $13,750 with Oldendorff, again no more details surfaced.

Asia
The Centurion Mevia (38,002 2021) was heard to have been fixed for 2/3 laden legs in the high 18,000s basis delivery Bahodopi. Elsewhere, the Elisar (36,817 2011) open WC India was placed on subjects at $12,000 for a trip to the Continent via the Gulf of Aden.

Market Fundamentals
Australia Crop Area Estimates Reduced for 2026

The Grains Industry Association of Western Australia reported on Friday that farmers will be planting less wheat and more canola this crop year. High fuel and fertiliser costs alongside lower grains prices have led to canola looking to be the more attractive crop for profitability. Total crop area estimates for this year are around 615,000 hectares lower than those seen for 2025 for Wheat, with increases in Canola and Barley not sufficient to offset this; total crop area estimates for the three grains is around 4% lower than last year, at ~7.7 million hectares vs. ~8 million hectares reported in July 2025. Western Australia accounted for around half of all Australian wheat, barley and canola exports in 2025, with 19.2 Mt being exported from Western Australia out of 35.9 Mt total, according to vessel tracking data.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve opened supported with pays on the Apr and May up to 32000 and 35000 respectively. The May v Jun spread continued to widen and strengthen up to +900, with the June range 33200-34200. Q3 was surprisingly thin today with only a few prints between 30900-31300 and even more so on the Q4, with a single clip clearing at 30850. Similarly, the Cals struggled for liquidity today as the Cal27 traded 25850, C28 22950 and 24500 sold on the C27+C28 strip.

PMX
PMX started the week opening flat initially before falling on the nearby. May traded at a high of 19150 then was hit down to 18650 while Jun printed from 19450 down to 19000, Jul traded 19350 to 18900 with little participation. Q3 saw less of a move printing 18700 down to 18500, Q4 held a narrow range between 17100 - 17050. CvP cal28 printed 9200 causing 13750 trading on the cal 28.

SMX + HANDY
A slow start to the week, as the curve traded flat and within a tight range in limited size. Apr traded in a few clips at 15650 and to a low of 15400 in small size, while May traded between 16900 – 17100, and Jun between 17000 – 17150 and Q2 at 16600. Q3 was supported, trading 16100 – 16200 and the Cal27 traded 12950. Handy market was relatively active trading out to Q3. May+jun traded 15000, Jun at 15300, Jul at 14500 and Q3 at 14250.

Carbon
European carbon allowances declined by 1.8% today, precipitated by a weaker auction result and in relatively quiet trading. During the assessment period, the benchmark Dec26 contract was trading at �76.13/eua, down �1.38.

This morning's EU Common compliance auction settled at �74.84/eua, below last Friday's daily spot futures level and setting a bearish tone for this morning's EUA futures trading. The weaker auction coincided with news that the Strait of Hormuz remains 'closed', which initially supported supported energy prices and, again, raised concerns about potential European energy demand destruction.

Australia Crop Area Estimates Reduced for 2026
The Grains Industry Association of Western Australia
reported on Friday that farmers will be planting less wheat
and more canola this crop year. High fuel and fertiliser costs
alongside lower grains prices have led to canola looking to
be the more attractive crop for proﬁtability. Total crop area
estimates for this year are around 615,000 hectares lower
than those seen for 2025 for Wheat, with increases in Canola
and Barley not suﬃcient to oﬀset this; total crop area
estimates for the three grains is around 4% lower than last
year, at ~7.7 million hectares vs. ~8 million hectares reported
in July 2025. Western Australia accounted for around half of
all Australian wheat, barley and canola exports in 2025, with
19.2 Mt being exported from Western Australia out of 35.9
Mt total, according to vessel tracking data.

ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场在4月20日当周延续升势，BDI上涨66点至2633，BCI领涨172点至4300，好望角型船5TC达38999美元。C3大西洋航线受 ballast收紧支撑走强，而C5太平洋航线基本持平。中小船型表现分化：巴拿马型增速放缓至仅涨1点，灵便型上涨234点至13571美元。FFA曲线显示近期走强但远期趋弱，特别是巴拿马型5-6月合约明显回调，反映市场对短期支撑与中长期需求前景存在分歧。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: 好望角型船继续主导市场涨势，BCI单日跳升172点至4300。C3大西洋航线因ballast收紧获得支撑，C9fronthaul暴涨3777点至66333美元。巴拿马型增速明显放缓，仅涨1点至1976，FFA曲线显示5月及Q2出现负增长，暗示市场对近期支撑能否持续存疑。灵便型表现稳健，7TC上涨234点，亚洲区域需求持续改善。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Capesize短期强势信号明确：C3航线+1.041至33.714，Atlantic tonnage收紧；C9 fronthaul暴涨+3777至66333。Supramax 11TC仅涨84点至17970，显示太平洋市场趋平衡。Handysize亚洲区域持续向好，7TC +234至13571，北部即期运力紧张。FFA曲线整体前高后低：cape Q3/Q4维持正增长但cal27-28转负，panamax各期全线负增长。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: C3航线为当前核心关注点，受Atlantic收紧支撑走强至33.714，FFA q3上涨至30.80。P1A_82(14.530)及P5_82(17.747)大西洋往返航线表现突出。Handysize亚洲航线HS6(+444)、HS7(+406)领涨。FFA上cape May/Jun价差扩大至+900，建议关注Q2/Q3跨月套利机会。Middle East地缘局势变化可能影响supramax后续走势。
